summary: Pressing material with ḥ-initial forms is split across ḥṣr 1 and ʕṣr.
rationale: Permitted lookup confirms ʕṣr has ḥṣəlle for grapes and g-ḥəṣró-way-no-la for curd; these overlap the paradigm and materials in ḥṣr 1. Preserve both inherited entries pending editorial consolidation, not automatic deletion.

data.turoyo: Kise du=ʕamro-wayne, saymənwanne lu=ḥṣoro daʕ=ʕənwe, d ḥəṣri aʕ=ʕənwe saymənne dibəs.
data.translation: Es waren Säcke aus Wolle, man machte sie für das Auspressen der Trauben, um die Trauben (darin) auszupressen und Traubensirup herzustellen.

rationale: Thin Infinitiv/1; second token supplies explicit genitival patient absent from the existing short Infinitiv quotation.

data.turoyo: Omər: "Qayəmno, aṯino, qṭəfli ʕənwe kome, məblili li maḥsarto, ḥṣirili w čikili b gawa di maḥsarto w daʕənno.
data.translation: Ich machte noch auf, pflückte schwarze Trauben, brachte sie zur Kelter, presste sie, tat sie in die Kelter hinein und kehrte zurück.

rationale: Thin Preterit/1; pronominal grape patient and pressing sequence.

data.turoyo: Bu sabab d i naqqa ḥreto d rawəxwo aʕle, fəšwole taqrib d ʕəsri yawme ʕal ḥaṣe, hama xayifo rahəṭ w azzeyo l bayn u bəstono, qṭəflele ʕənwe w disa ḥṣirile bi maḥsarto w fayəš məqdar d ḥamšaḥṣar yawme ḥrene bu ʕaḏabano.
data.translation: Weil nun das vorige Mal der Kerl, der auf mir ritt, fast zwanzig Tage auf meinem Rücken geblieben war, lief ich diesmal gleich in den Garten, pflückte mir Trauben und presste sie in der Kelter; und so blieb ich nur fünfzehn Tage in dieser Qual.

rationale: Thin Preterit/1; winepress location and repeated pressing.

summary: All nine occurrences fit existing I.1 pressing/squeezing. Grapes and curd extend the patient material without a new technical sense.
The squeezed material is an NP or patient suffix; hands are b-marked instruments and the winepress is a b-marked location. Expelled blood or liquid need not be a verb argument.
Finite pressing and Infinitiv purpose/genitive constructions share the grape patient. Repeated finite tokens at JL 14.9/8 form one inherited context and are not independent examples.
The ḥ/ʕ root split is editorially unresolved. Root-final r assimilation before -le explains ḥṣəlle without a new ḥṣl root.
JL 20.7/45 supplies German 'hielt den Daumen', while the inherited English quotation says 'kept the needle'. This is a translation discrepancy; the source Turoyo itself elides the held object.
Consolidate ḥṣr 1 and ʕṣr or specify the intended dialectal/root distinction; keep source spellings unchanged.
In JL 14.9/8 does -nne refer to grapes or raisins, and what is the exact person segmentation of ḥəṣrənwanne? The generic German should not decide the morphology alone.

Correct the inherited JL 20.7.44–45 translation's 'kept the needle' against the edition's thumb reading after checking the complete two-verse quotation; no missing verse translation has been fabricated.
Remove the doubled r in Ausprressen
rationale: Ausprressen has an extra r. The supplied JL 17.6.1 translation reads Auspressen; the longer glossary quotation also spells it correctly on its second occurrence.
